label: three-arm-tc-subsidy
_why: THE FIRST BATCH ON THE SAVEGAME INSTRUMENT (ROADMAP step 3.5), and the first three-arm comparison of the shipped mod. Four questions: (1) is VANILLA still what it was - same economy, same wall clock - measured against the earlier vanilla sessions, which is what separates a telemetry tax from a mod tax; (2) how far the mod is from vanilla on GDP, stability and speed; (3) whether MANDATING TRADE-CENTRE SUBSIDIES buys more trade, and what it costs in GDP, in budget share and in bankruptcies; (4) whether the save summaries agree with the log telemetry on GDP, building counts and population - the alignment gate that must pass before any state-of-process metric is moved off the logs.
_arms: vanilla = {kind: control} - vanilla + telemetry, ZERO gameplay content (build.ps1 throws if handed content). mod = {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.json} - the shipped mod, 217 technologies, 100 tier buildings, trade centre at must_have. mod_no_tc = {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.no_tc_subsidy.json} - byte-identical to `mod` EXCEPT six lines: building_trade_center = must_have removed from all six administrative AI strategies. VERIFIED by a full-tree diff of the two builds: only those six lines plus the build timestamp differ. Vanilla's own ai_strategy_default subsidises power_plant/railway/port and NOT trade centres, so this genuinely withdraws the mandate rather than falling back to a default that would reinstate it.
_order: 2.1-2.2-2.3-2.1-2.2-2.3, interleaved by user instruction rather than blocked by arm, so that any drift in machine state over ~16 hours (thermal, background load, time of day) falls on all three arms equally instead of on whichever ran last.
_metrics: country_state + population = per-country GDP, foreign-owned GDP, market, and workforce composition (ROADMAP step 4's sharpest test). tech_log = every acquisition to the day, which a save can never give - a save shows what is HELD, never when it arrived. treasury = the budget panel per country, and it is the one that carries GetSubsidiesExpenses and the TRADE line (market trade capacity + trade-centre count and levels) - the direct instrument for question 3. events = bankruptcy (on_country_default), war, peace. building_inventory is a 1836-only boot snapshot and is kept for continuity with earlier sessions.
_saves: AUTOSAVES ARE NOW AN INSTRUMENT, not just crash insurance: archived concurrently, then melted and summarised between runs (tools/harvest_saves.ps1 -> one save_state_summary.mjs JSON per save). That gives ANNUAL per-country GDP / buildings-by-type / professions / technologies-held / per-building SUBSIDY SPEND, against the log telemetry's 12 dump dates.
_cadence: YEARLY, not quarterly - and the reason is this batch's own wall-clock question. Writing a 40-55 MB autosave stalls the engine, so 400 quarterly saves would add an estimated 4-13% to every run and pollute exactly the number question (1) is asking for. Yearly is also the cadence the earlier VANILLA sessions used (20260805_234555, 20260806_110926), which makes vanilla-now directly comparable to vanilla-then on this axis. Quarterly is measured-feasible on the consumer side (melt+extract streams end to end at ~5 s per save, so 4 workers drain a century in ~8 min) and is the right choice for a batch whose question is not wall clock.
_cost: 6 runs x 100 in-game years. Measured on 20260811_020843: 2h36 per mod run, and ~2h20 for a vanilla run of the same span. Budget ~15h of game time plus ~2 min of save harvest per run and ~1 min of build. timeout_minutes 330 per run, as the last full-length batch used.
_disk: ~100 saves per run at ~40 MB = ~4 GB standing during a run, drained to a ~120 MB summary set plus ONE kept save per run (the escape hatch for questions the schema did not anticipate). The archiver stops itself if free space falls below 8 GB.
